evidence: Lowering byte-width precision (e.g. FP8 on H100; FP4 only on Blackwell-class parts) does not reduce the underlying algorithmic operation count (the usual 2 × params × tokens FLOPs are approximately unchanged — the matmuls still multiply the same matrices); it lowers the bytes transferred/stored and can raise the effective accelerator throughput (8-bit tensor cores run at a higher peak rate).
issue: The text states that FP8 lowers the bytes transferred and raises the effective accelerator throughput. This is true for weight reads (decode), but for compute-bound phases (prefill), H100 Tensor Cores operate at the same FLOPs/s for FP16 and FP8. FP8 primarily benefits the memory-bound regime (decoding) by halving the weight bytes, but does not double compute FLOPs/s for dense FP8 matmuls compared to dense FP16. This claim is confusing and potentially misleading.
fix_instruction: Update to state: 'FP8 lowers the bytes transferred/stored, which significantly improves bandwidth-bound decode performance. For compute-bound prefill, H100 Tensor Cores typically deliver the same FLOPs/s for FP16 and FP8, so throughput gains are limited to memory efficiency (fewer bytes to load per calculation).'
